Commun. 23, 83 (1977) on (4s nd) 1D2 exists but is paywalled). Kurucz's semi-empirical calculation (kurucz.harvard.edu/atoms/3000/life3000.lab) lists e.g. 29.8 ns (5s 1S0), 14.4 ns (4d 1D2), 52 ns (5p 3P), not entered because it misses the measured 4s4p 1P1 lifetime by 20 %.

Blagoev et al. 2004 (Phys. Scr. 69, 433) full text: restricted on ORBi and IOP; its lifetimes are entered second-hand from the Kurucz list. Kerkhoff et al. 1980: only the first two pages (Springer preview, with Table 1) were read; the 4s6d 3D1 row is cut off there.

A values for lines other than the two 3P-3S1 / 3P-3D multiplets and the ground-state lines (4s5s 3S1 - 4snp 3P, 4s4p 1P1 - 4sns 1S0 / 4snd 1D2, 3P - 4sns 3S1 / 4snd 3D with n >= 5): no measured branching ratios located (LS coupling would give them from the measured lifetimes, not entered because that is a model).
67Zn hyperfine constants of 4s4d 3D and higher levels: not located. 65Zn (radioactive) constants of Byron et al. 1964 not entered.
Raw isotope shifts of the 481 nm line by Campbell, Billowes, Grant (J. Phys. B 30, 2351 (1997)) and Yang et al.: not opened; the COLLAPS values of Xie et al. 2019 are entered instead.
Measured Lande g factors: none beyond the values already in the NIST ASD levels file.
conflicts: 67Zn 4s4p 3P1 hyperfine constants: A = 608.922(3), B = -18.995(10) MHz (Waldherr et al. 2026, laser fluorescence) vs A = 609.086(1), B = -18.782(8) MHz (Byron et al. 1964, double resonance); the F=5/2-3/2 interval differs by 0.77 MHz, reason unknown.
307.6 nm isotope shifts: new kHz-level values vs Campbell et al.: 68-64 1362.390(3) vs 1365.2(1.4) MHz and 70-64 1958.358(7) vs 1962.2(1.7) MHz (2 sigma).
67Zn 1P1 magnetic hyperfine constant: 20(2) MHz (Roeser 2024) vs 17.7(5) MHz (Kowalski & Traeger).
213.9 nm natural linewidth: 110.5(1.4) MHz measured (tau = 1.440(18) ns) vs 114 MHz from the NIST A value (7.14e8 s^-1, tau = 1.40 ns) vs 71 MHz quoted by Bandarupally et al. 2023.
307.6 nm linewidth: 6 kHz (theory, quoted by Bueki 2021 and Moeller 2025; tau ~ 26 us) vs 4 kHz (Bandarupally 2023); the task brief assumed ~4 kHz.

4s4p 3P1 lifetime: the only direct measurement, 20(2) us (Byron et al. 1964, double resonance with wall-collision correction), is shorter than 26 us (NIST A = 3.8e4 s^-1, accuracy B) and 30 us (A = 3.29e4 s^-1 recommended by Roederer & Lawler 2012 from Reader et al. 1980); theory log gf ranges from -3.72 to -3.89 (Roederer & Lawler). The existing ~26 us entry was kept as primary because the measurement is 60 years old.
67Zn 4s4p 3P2 hyperfine constants: atomic-beam 531.987(5) / 35.806(5) MHz (Lurio 1962) vs collinear-laser 531.2(11) / 41(7) MHz (Wraith et al. 2017); consistent, atomic-beam values kept.

Triplet lifetimes: Kerkhoff et al. 1980 vs Blagoev et al. 2004 (second-hand): 4d 3D 6.2-6.4(3) vs 6.1(4) ns, 6s 3S1 22.1(1.1) vs 22.3(7), 5d 3D 13.3-14.3(7) vs 15.0(6), 7s 3S1 46.9(2.3) vs 50(5), 6d 3D2 28.4(2.0) vs 30.0(12) ns; all consistent. Older non-selective results quoted by Kerkhoff differ strongly (e.g. 6s 3S1: 13(2) ns beam-foil, 30(4) ns electron excitation). The Kurucz list prints Kerkhoff's 4d uncertainties as 0.2 ns, the paper prints 0.3 ns.
The Kurucz hyperfine input file prints B(67Zn, 3P1) = -19.782 MHz for Byron et al. 1964; the Physical Review abstract prints -18.782(8) MHz (and A = 609.086(2), not (1)).
notes: Conventions. (1) Isotope-shift keys 'a-b' mean nu(a) - nu(b), all relative to 64Zn as printed; 67Zn values are hyperfine centres of gravity. (2) Fields beyond SCHEMA.md: natural_linewidth_*, photoionization, top-level 'rydberg' (ionization limit) and 'conflicts'. (3) rme_J_ea0 values are derived here from lifetimes (schema convention, branching to the ground state taken as 1); the 307.6 nm one rests on an approximate, uncited lifetime. (4) The 307.6 nm frequency_THz is a natural-mixture Doppler centre and is flagged 'not verified' in its source string so that the pipeline ignores it. (5) Zinc has far less modern laser-spectroscopy data than Cd or Hg: only the two ground-state lines have been measured with lasers. (6) Added 2026-10-01 (second pass): lifetimes of the 4sns 3S1 (n = 5-8) and 4snd 3D (n = 4-7) levels (Kerkhoff et al. 1980 read directly in the Springer two-page preview; Blagoev et al. 2004 second-hand from Kurucz's life3000.lab), 67Zn hyperfine constants of 4s4p 3P2 and 4s5s 3S1, isotope shifts of the 481.2 nm line relative to 68Zn (keys 'A-68' = nu(A) - nu(68), unc = statistical error only), and lifetime-normalised A values of the 3P-3S1 and 3P-3D multiplets (LS-coupling branching, see the notes). NIST lists 4s7d 3D1 and 3D2 at the same energy 72626.0 cm^-1: the entries are told apart by J only.
